target: production-built API and Cloud Nest applications over loopback with separate disposable PostgreSQL 16 databases
identities: Synthetic superadmin and coordinator database rows; signed tokens intentionally carry mismatched role claims.
checks: A database superadmin can create definitions across two companies and list both, update a definition, and soft-deactivate it.
A coordinator token claiming superadmin is resolved as coordinator from PostgreSQL; a forged company filter cannot reveal another tenant's flow.
A coordinator's forged foreign-company create is scoped to its own company; a foreign definition update returns no record.
A superadmin creates and approves a version; later edits to the approved version receive HTTP 400.
Version list queries are global for the superadmin and limited to the coordinator's database company despite a forged filter.
Superadmin availability permission create/read/disable and intent mapping create/read/removal persist; coordinator cross-company permission and mapping writes receive HTTP 400.
A superadmin assigns an unowned legacy flow to a company and reads it under its new owner.
A second Prisma client confirms the approved version, authenticated creator, disabled permission and mapping removal persisted.
cleanup: Both dedicated UAT databases were dropped; API and Cloud child processes exited; temporary data directory was removed; the reused PostgreSQL cluster was stopped with its pre-existing databases preserved.
external_traffic: none; test requests used loopback services and PostgreSQL only, with no customer/provider credentials or data
scope: This closes the four superadmin flow-configuration API matrix rows only. The corresponding Web role rows and broader CRUD matrix remain open.
